This question involves recursive methods in a class named `StringAndSearch`. The methods must be recursive; a solution that uses a loop to do the work will not earn full credit.

**(a)** Write the method `removeChar`, which returns a new string that contains the characters of `s` in their original order, with every occurrence of the character `c` removed.

```java
public static String removeChar(String s, char c)
```

Examples:

| Call | Returns |
|---|---|
| `removeChar("banana", 'a')` | `"bnn"` |
| `removeChar("xyz", 'a')` | `"xyz"` |
| `removeChar("aaa", 'a')` | `""` |

**(b)** Write the method `findFirst`, which uses recursion to return the index of the **first** occurrence of `t` in the sorted (ascending) array `a` within the range `a[lo]` through `a[hi]`, inclusive, or -1 if `t` does not appear in that range. The array may contain duplicate values. The method should use a binary-search strategy (it should not examine every element).

```java
/** Precondition: a is sorted in ascending order; 0 <= lo and hi < a.length (but lo > hi is possible) */
public static int findFirst(int[] a, int t, int lo, int hi)
```

For example, if `arr` is {1, 3, 3, 3, 5, 8, 8, 9}, then `findFirst(arr, 3, 0, 7)` returns 1, `findFirst(arr, 8, 0, 7)` returns 5, and `findFirst(arr, 4, 0, 7)` returns -1.

rubric.description: (a) Base case: returns the empty string when `s` is empty
(a) When the first character equals `c`, recurs on the rest of the string without that character
(a) Otherwise returns the first character concatenated with the result of the recursive call on the rest
(a) Recursive calls make progress toward the base case (for example `s.substring(1)`), and no loops are used
(b) Computes a middle index and recurs on the correct half when `a[mid]` is less than or greater than `t`
(b) When `a[mid]` equals `t`, searches the left part for an earlier occurrence and returns that index if there is one, and otherwise returns `mid`

This question involves two recursive methods. Both methods must be recursive; a solution that uses a loop to do the work will not earn full credit.

**(a)** A hiker climbs a staircase and, on each move, climbs 1, 2 or 3 steps. Write the method `ways`, which returns the number of different sequences of moves that climb exactly `n` steps. A sequence is different if the numbers of steps in its moves are in a different order. Climbing zero steps can be done in exactly one way (making no moves), and a negative number of steps cannot be climbed at all.

```java
public static int ways(int n)
```

For example, `ways(3)` returns 4, since the possible sequences are 1+1+1, 1+2, 2+1 and 3. Also `ways(4)` returns 7 and `ways(5)` returns 13.

**(b)** Write the method `canMake`, which returns true if some collection of the values in `vals[index]` through the end of the array (each value used at most once) adds up to exactly `target`, and false otherwise. A collection of no values has a sum of 0. All of the values in `vals` and the value of `target` are non-negative.

```java
/** Precondition: 0 <= index and target >= 0 */
public static boolean canMake(int[] vals, int index, int target)
```

For example, if `v` is {3, 9, 8, 4}, then `canMake(v, 0, 12)` returns true (3 + 9, or 8 + 4), `canMake(v, 0, 5)` returns false, and `canMake(v, 2, 12)` returns true (8 + 4).

rubric.description: (a) Base cases: returns 0 for a negative argument and 1 for zero
(a) Adds the results of the three calls and returns the sum
(b) Returns true when `target` is 0 (before checking whether values remain)
(b) Returns false when there are no values left (`index` is past the end), without accessing the array out of bounds
(b) Makes the recursive call that uses `vals[index]`: with `target - vals[index]` and `index + 1`
(b) Makes the recursive call that skips `vals[index]` and combines the two results so that the method returns true if either one is true
